Thank you for taking the time to leave your feedback. I am sorry to hear that you were disappointed with your recent experience and for the delay in being able to offer you an appointment. We appreciate you bringing this to our attention.

Demand for appointments remains extremely high and, unfortunately, this can sometimes mean that routine telephone appointments are booked several weeks in advance. I do apologise that you had to wait three weeks for the scheduled call.

I have looked into the matter you raised regarding the telephone consultation on the 10th at 10:10am. Our records indicate that the pharmacist did attempt to call your number on two occasions at the time of the appointment, however the calls went to voicemail/answerphone. We understand how frustrating it must have been to feel that the call had not been made when you had been waiting for it, and I am sorry for the inconvenience this caused.

When a call is not successfully connected, the appointment is unfortunately recorded as a missed consultation and we have to offer the next available routine appointment, which is why the next date offered was later in April.

We are sorry that your experience with the reception team left you feeling that your concerns were not fully acknowledged. This was certainly not our intention and we will remind our team of the importance of explaining these situations clearly and sympathetically.

Thank you again for raising this with us. We do hope that your next contact with the practice is a more positive experience.

Yours sincerely,
Judith Goldsworthy
